cim: UNESCO Santiago secures international funding to strengthen journalist
cim_eredeti: UNESCO Santiago secures international funding to strengthen journalist
szoveg_eredeti:
The UNESCO Regional Office in Santiago is moving forward with the implementation of two projects funded by the Organization’s intergovernmental programmes, aimed at addressing current challenges related to the right to information, freedom of expression and transformations in the digital environment.

These initiatives will help strengthen knowledge generation, the development of tools and the capacities of different stakeholders to address two priority areas: the safety of journalists, with particular attention to the risks faced by women, and media and information literacy in a context shaped by the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI).

With national and regional scope, respectively, both projects will contribute to promoting access to reliable information, the exercise of fundamental rights and the building of more inclusive and democratic knowledge societies.

The project “Monitoring and analysis system for the safety of journalists in Chile”, approved during the 69th meeting of the Bureau of the Intergovernmental Council of the International Programme for the Development of Communication (IPDC), held on 19 June 2025, aims to strengthen national capacities to record, monitor and analyse attacks against journalists.

Developed together with the Observatory on the Right to Communication (ODC), the initiative includes the development of a methodology for recording attacks against the press, the systematization of information on attacks that have occurred in Chile since 2020, and the creation of a digital platform bringing together data disaggregated by type of attack, the gender and profile of victims and perpetrators, geographical location, and other variables.

The project also includes specific research on the safety of women journalists in Chile, with the aim of identifying differentiated risks and developing recommendations to strengthen mechanisms for prevention, monitoring and combating impunity.

Its implementation will follow a participatory, multi-stakeholder approach involving civil society organizations, media representatives, academic institutions, public bodies and other stakeholders linked to the protection of freedom of expression. At least 60% of direct beneficiaries will be women.

Through these actions, the project seeks to improve the availability of information on the threats facing journalistic work and to provide tools that facilitate their monitoring and analysis, contributing to a more informed and coordinated response by the stakeholders involved.

As part of the commemoration of the 25th anniversary of the Information for All Programme (IFAP), the UNESCO Regional Office in Santiago was selected to implement one of the three initiatives that will receive support from the Programme in 2026, alongside projects led from West Africa and the Caribbean.

The initiative seeks to strengthen critical artificial intelligence literacy among teachers, students and education authorities in Latin America and the Caribbean, promoting the development of capacities to understand, evaluate and use these technologies ethically, critically and responsibly.

The project will be implemented through UNESCO’s Observatory on Artificial Intelligence in Education for Latin America and the Caribbean, with the aim of generating knowledge and supporting capacity-building across the region.

The main expected outcomes include regional seminars in Montevideo and Santiago; the preparation of an evidence-based regional document on media and information literacy and artificial intelligence in education; and strengthened capacities to advance policies, initiatives and tools that promote the responsible use of these technologies.

This article is related to the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals.
